items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: they’re reforming the Salt City Six up on Memory Lane up in Syracuse. Jack Maheu, Will Alger, trumpet player Paul Squire, my father on piano

ctx.x: That’s okay. Hey you don’t have to like everything. Well it seems like you must have been getting to a point where you decided well this is what I’m going to do.

Well as I said, well okay, between my junior and senior year of high school of course I discovered the joys of physical relationships with women along that period of time. And my girlfriend at the time happened to be the prettiest girl in the school. But I had played, at the age of 15, now I had gotten mononucleosis and had to stay home for two weeks. Mono is a blood — they call it “kissing disease” actually. So anyway, as soon as I got released from that I’m going back to school and Arnie Koch from — they’re…

to that, when I was 14. But let me preface that by saying that because my eyes were bad at that time we used to go to New York. And we’d go to the Taft Hotel when Vincent Lopez’s band was playing. Because my father — we would stay at the Taft and they used to have a thing called “Shake the Maracas” contest, which was a radio show. And they had me sit in on drums at 14. I’ve got photos of it. And man I was more nervous than a prostitute in church. Or you could say a whore in church. But you can edit that too. So…
